batch_strategy: Boundary repair with nitrogen, carbonyl, loading, and compact-control contrasts

choices.reason: Compact m130 at weak ratio and low sample volume provides a donor-free calibration anchor. It helps keep tail corrections localized, consistent with compact behavior in 382ed88009a39dd77794 and 1e23400bcfdf6336d604.

Weak-ratio m11 supplies the low-strength endpoint for a nitrogen-containing scaffold. It tests whether the delayed strong-ratio basic-nitrogen behavior in 49201b5817f204116f7f and 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4 transfers across ratio.
This compact heavy-halogen m139 strong-ratio cell checks whether compact behavior persists at stronger solvent, complementing 72f4152617833b191b9a and 649a78c668441818d1bc.

Low-ratio m93 provides an acceptor-rich but compact reference before applying strong-ratio carbonyl corrections. It helps separate ordinary endpoint movement from the tails seen in 30dcf629a319b1b39ea6 and d626f5ddb709bc11257a.
M50 is a donor-free hydrophobic control at weak ratio and fixed loading. Its narrow predicted range constrains generalization of polar-tail corrections into ordinary rows.

The strong-ratio m143 condition has a broad predicted interval and probes a halogenated aromatic aldehyde boundary. It tests whether carbonyl completion tails extend into this scaffold family, as suggested by observed m193 and m178 tails.

Strong-ratio m110 samples an aromatic ether scaffold with substantial predicted endpoint spread. It provides a non-donor contrast for deciding whether broad intervals reflect genuine completion tails or model extrapolation.

M148 is a compact heavy-halogen control at strong ratio and moderate sample volume. It checks localization of the large corrections seen in delayed polar rows against the compact behavior in 72f4152617833b191b9a.

M168 is a high-width multifunctional carbonyl at 5/1 and fixed loading solvent. Its label can separate a smooth carbonyl endpoint response from localized tail regimes observed in e9a7d193dc3d83532c1f and 89cd51ad92ae6285b501.

This m87 10/1 ester condition samples a strong-ratio acceptor-rich family with moderate predicted spread. It tests whether completion broadening appears without the extreme loading-solvent plugs associated with 3b400f57f8dcc4cdbd83.
M156 provides a compact fluorinated heavy-atom control under PE at 10/1. It helps prevent aromatic carbonyl-tail corrections from transferring to donor-free structures.
Weak-ratio m80 gives a low-complexity ester baseline at moderate sample volume. It anchors ordinary acceptor-rich behavior before comparing stronger-ratio and loading-dependent ester tails.
Strong-ratio m79 tests a compact ester/halogen neighborhood at high loading amount. It helps determine whether loading amount alone is sufficient to create tails like those in 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4.

M12 at 20/1 PE is a hydrophobic high-ratio control with a wide predicted interval. Its label can identify whether broad model uncertainty corresponds to genuine solvent response in donor-free structures.
M112 at 10/1 with a 600 ul plug probes loading-solvent volume in a heavy-atom aromatic ether. It tests whether plug effects remain compact or generate a localized completion displacement.

Strong-ratio m11 supplies the opposite end of the nitrogen response curve from 0634486d18ed767b5150. The pair can distinguish a smooth ratio effect from a scaffold-specific transition using the measured nitrogen failures in 49201b5817f204116f7f and 35f2be5f5aa14265e8a4.
M14 is a donor-free hydrophobic strong-ratio control with a narrow predicted interval. It constrains solvent-strength calibration outside delayed nitrogen and carbonyl families.
Weak-ratio m8 supplies a heteroaromatic ether anchor at high sample volume. It tests whether modest acceptor content remains compact before stronger-ratio corrections are applied.
M122 at 1/1 provides a low-ratio aromatic ether reference with moderate loading amount. It supports local calibration of onset and completion in donor-free heteroatom scaffolds.

M166 at 2/1 is a multifunctional carbonyl condition with broad predicted V2 spread. It probes whether completion broadening begins at intermediate ratio, complementing the observed strong-ratio m166 result e9a7d193dc3d83532c1f.
M215 provides a compact fused-aromatic control at 1/1 with a larger loading-solvent volume. It tests loading-solvent effects without donor or strong acceptor functionality.
M12 at 50/1 PE extends the donor-free hydrophobic ratio range. Comparing it with 9c200a8ce916cb2ac23 tests whether high-ratio endpoint changes are scaffold-general or localized to polar families.
M179 is a compact cyclic carbonyl anchor at 1/1. It helps distinguish ordinary carbonyl retention from completion tails observed in 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4 and f31a89256d8ee4192d55.

M169 adds a halogenated ketone at intermediate ratio and fixed loading. It tests whether carbonyl onset and completion shift together or separate, as in the endpoint-separated behavior motivating H_ONSET_ENDPOINT.

Strong-ratio m124 probes a fused aromatic ether with moderate predicted spread. It supplies a non-donor comparison for strong-ratio aromatic behavior seen in f38088920e6edd19a62f and 22300151ccec3f1f1c24.
M192 at 20/1 with a 400 ul plug targets a halogenated aldehyde boundary. It can test whether completion tails are ratio-driven or require larger loading-solvent volumes.
This m184 strong-ratio aldehyde condition uses a 500 ul plug and moderate sample volume. It extends the halogenated carbonyl family into a loading-solvent regime adjacent to measured m184 controls.

M26 at 20/1 and 150 ul samples a simple aromatic diketone-like scaffold with broad predicted endpoints. It tests whether acceptor-rich completion tails generalize beyond multifunctional ester families.
M188 at 1/1 is a weak-ratio halogenated aldehyde anchor. It helps locate the ratio threshold for carbonyl completion growth before interpreting high-width strong-ratio m143 and m192 cells.
M4 is a donor-free fused aromatic control at weak ratio and moderate loading-solvent volume. It constrains structural-size effects separately from polar adsorption corrections.
M16 is a weak-ratio compact ester reference at high sample volume. It provides a baseline for loading-volume effects in acceptor-rich but non-tail conditions.
M215 at 10/1 extends the compact fused-aromatic control to stronger solvent and larger loading-solvent volume. It tests whether compact calibration remains stable across ratio and plug changes.

hypotheses.content: Basic and heteroaromatic nitrogen scaffolds have scaffold-specific, ratio-dependent onset and completion transitions that do not transfer reliably from nitrogen count or generic polarity descriptors.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Matched weak and strong ratio cells can teach separate scaffold-conditioned V1 and V2 transitions instead of one global nitrogen correction.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Does the m11 ratio response follow the m211 and m216 transition pattern, or require a distinct scaffold-specific representation?

hypotheses.content: Large V2 completion tails are localized to scaffold, ratio, and loading-solvent neighborhoods; similar predicted structures can enter very different endpoint regimes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: High-width carbonyl, ether, and nitrogen contrasts can localize V2 corrections and reduce broad overcorrection across ordinary rows.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which acceptor-rich families show smooth tail growth, and which show a ratio or loading-solvent completion switch?

hypotheses.content: Donor-containing aromatic structures separate into geometry-specific adsorption regimes; donor count alone does not determine whether V1 is delayed, V2 develops a tail, or both endpoints remain compact.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: The generalization target contains donor-containing rows with different geometries, so local alcohol contrasts can prevent a donor-wide offset.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do attachment geometry and fused-ring structure predict the split between compact and delayed donor behavior?

hypotheses.content: Loading amount, sample volume, loading-solvent volume, and ratio interact non-smoothly in tail-prone scaffolds, with V2 often more sensitive than V1.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Loading contrasts teach whether the loading features move V1, V2, or the interval width within specific chemical families.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Are the large loading effects reproducible within a scaffold family or confined to particular ratio and plug-volume cells?

hypotheses.content: Carbonyl, ester, and related acceptor-rich families can show condition-dependent V1 changes that are not proportional to V2 changes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Endpoint-separated labels improve joint V1/V2 calibration and prevent completion-tail corrections from being applied to onset errors.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Which simple halogenated and aromatic carbonyls show an onset threshold while their completion remains locally smooth?

hypotheses.content: Donor-free hydrophobic and heavy-atom structures provide necessary compact calibration anchors across solvent ratio and loading changes.
hypotheses.why_it_matters_for_model_learning: Compact anchors constrain the retrained model against spreading large polar-tail corrections into the much larger ordinary portion of the Row-distribution.
hypotheses.next_discriminating_question: Do donor-free fused and heavy-halogen structures remain compact at stronger ratios and altered loading, or are there localized exceptions?

feedback_interpretation: Recent feedback strengthened the view that endpoint errors are scaffold- and condition-specific. The m216 measurements c5185bd663026c64c816, 07933c8c797c30bb0e8e, and 9cd02352c2ed7a3e2321 show a pronounced ratio response, while m211 measurements ecd17c7ea435a1e33f6b, d119d77f545c029deace, and 434e465cfa7e0034f233 follow a different curve. The m193 cells 69b09343d0b9995c3ae4, 3b400f57f8dcc4cdbd83, and c45057c2cab40f4fa2be show strong completion sensitivity, whereas m203 measurements 9ed7c1fb1c2cc499bbf9 and 66747ae127e03516ffda show that loading can move V1 without a comparable V2 displacement. The selected batch therefore emphasizes ratio boundaries, carbonyl completion, and loading contrasts while retaining compact controls.
batch_rationale: The batch spans nitrogen response extremes, high-width carbonyl and ether conditions, loading-solvent and sample-volume contrasts, and multiple donor-free compact controls. The paired weak and strong ratio cells can repair scaffold-specific transitions; the carbonyl and ester cells target large V2 losses; the controls constrain the correction field across ordinary hydrophobic and heavy-atom rows. This combination should improve generalization across both the high-loss delayed subset and the much larger compact portion of the Row-distribution.
